brief: A resort hotel on the bluff above the bay: a three-storey cream-yellow brick block with white trim, a colonnaded two-storey entrance portico with a balcony, rows of sash windows under a bracketed cornice, a long porch, and a 1990s balconied wing behind. Four photos. Older than 1970: the grand resort hotel on the bay is a 19th-century type (the town's model). Foundations taken deeper than needed (spec rule 4).

facade.notes: Stafford's Perry Hotel (Petoskey MI, 1899): a three-storey cream-yellow brick resort hotel with white quoins and a bracketed cornice, a two-storey columned portico with a balcony at the corner entrance, a long wraparound veranda with hanging flower baskets and bunting; on the bluff at the edge of downtown

why.note: the 1890s railroad resort hotel of northern Michigan: verandas for the summer visitors from Chicago and Detroit
